activities.title: Historic Dockyard
activities.description: Wander the free entry areas of one of the world's greatest naval heritage sites, including harbour views and the exterior of iconic ships like HMS Victory and HMS Warrior.

activities.title: Southsea Common
activities.description: 100 acres of open seafront parkland stretching from Clarence Pier to Southsea Castle. Perfect for kite flying, picnics and informal sports with stunning views across the Solent.

activities.title: Rose Gardens
activities.description: Beautifully maintained formal gardens near the seafront, featuring colourful rose beds and a peaceful atmosphere year-round.

activities.title: Clarence Pier
activities.description: Portsmouth's iconic western seafront pier and amusement park — rides, arcades and the Big Wheel with views across the Solent. Free to walk around and enjoy the atmosphere.

activities.title: Adventure Golf
activities.description: A classic seaside crazy golf course on Southsea seafront — great fun for all ages with a variety of themed holes.

activities.title: South Parade Pier
activities.description: Stroll out over the Solent on one of England's last remaining traditional seaside piers, built in 1908. A beloved Portsmouth landmark with views back to the seafront.

activities.title: Hilsea Lines
activities.description: 80 hectares of ancient Napoleonic fortifications surrounded by woodland, meadows and brackish lakes. A hidden gem for walkers and cyclists, with ranger-led talks about military history and local wildlife.

activities.title: Splash Park
activities.description: A free-access water play area on Southsea Common — a summertime favourite for families with jets, sprays and splash zones.

activities.title: Volleyball Courts
activities.description: Free public beach volleyball courts on Southsea seafront. Drop in for a casual game or watch others play against the backdrop of the Solent.

activities.title: Victoria Park
activities.description: Portsmouth's oldest park, featuring formal Victorian gardens, a decorative bandstand, war memorial, aviary and ornamental pond. A tranquil green retreat in the heart of the city.

activities.title: Highland Cemetery
activities.description: A peaceful and historically significant Victorian cemetery, rich in architectural interest and local heritage. A surprisingly serene green space worth exploring.

activities.title: Southsea Beach
activities.description: Miles of pebble shoreline stretching along the southern coast of Portsea Island, with spectacular views across the Solent to the Isle of Wight. Ideal for walks, swimming and skimming stones.

activities.title: Canoe Lake Park
activities.description: A charming ornamental lake and park slightly set back from the seafront. Famous for its white swan pedalos and rowing boats, large children's play area with zip wire, sandpit and crazy golf.

activities.title: Eastney Beach
activities.description: A wilder, more rugged beach at the southeastern tip of Portsea Island with scattered gorse, pebble shores and big skies. Ideal for sunset walks, birdwatching and quiet reflection.

activities.title: Farlington Marshes
activities.description: A 123-hectare nature reserve managed by the Hampshire Wildlife Trust. Walk the 2.5-mile circular trail around internationally significant wetlands, spotting avocets, brent geese, short-eared owls and more.

activities.title: Portsmouth Museum & Art Gallery
activities.description: Free permanent collections spanning local history, archaeology and fine art — including a celebrated Sherlock Holmes exhibition — housed in a handsome Victorian building in Museum Road.

activities.title: Cumberland House Natural History Museum
activities.description: A free natural history museum in Southsea with a butterfly house, freshwater aquarium and exhibits on local wildlife and fossils — a great family visit all year round.

activities.title: Southsea Castle
activities.description: Visit Henry VIII's coastal fort built in 1544. Explore the grounds, gun platform and ramparts with spectacular seaward views, and learn about the sinking of the Mary Rose watched from here.

activities.title: Fort Nelson
activities.description: A free Royal Armouries museum on Portsdown Hill housing over 350 historic guns. Explore how this Victorian fort would have been garrisoned in the 1890s, with panoramic views over Portsmouth Harbour.

activities.title: Portsdown Hill
activities.description: A chalk ridge north of the city offering sweeping panoramic views across the whole of Portsmouth, the harbour, Spithead and the Isle of Wight. Popular with walkers, cyclists and picnickers.

activities.title: Millennium Promenade
activities.description: A waymarked coastal walk through the city's history, with chain motifs embedded in the pavement telling stories of famous naval battles and momentous Portsmouth events.

activities.title: Langstone Harbour Waterside Walk
activities.description: A spectacular 14-mile circular walk around the entirety of Langstone Harbour, starting from Ferry Point at Eastney. One of Portsmouth's finest and most rewarding walks.

activities.title: Southsea Skatepark
activities.description: A free public skatepark on Southsea Common with ramps, bowls and rails suitable for all skill levels. A lively spot to skate or simply watch.

activities.title: Ship-Spotting from the Harbour
activities.description: Watch an ever-changing parade of ferries, naval vessels, cruise ships and cargo ships — including the spectacular Brittany Ferries departures — from the Hot Walls or the harbour mouth.

activities.title: Old Portsmouth & the Camber
activities.description: Wander the cobbled streets of Portsmouth's ancient heart — the Round Tower, Square Tower, Hot Walls and the atmospheric Camber Dock. One of the most historically rich walks in the city.

activities.title: Tour HMS Victory
activities.description: Step aboard Nelson's flagship, the world's oldest naval vessel still in commission. Walk the gun decks, see the spot where Nelson fell, and explore 250 years of naval history.

activities.title: Step aboard HMS Warrior
activities.description: Britain's first iron-hulled, armoured warship from 1861. Walk her vast decks, explore the engine room and discover how she changed naval warfare forever.

activities.title: Visit the Mary Rose Museum
activities.description: Henry VIII's flagship, raised from the Solent after 437 years. An extraordinary preservation triumph — see the hull and thousands of Tudor artefacts in a specially designed museum.

activities.title: National Museum of the Royal Navy
activities.description: Three floors of immersive naval history spanning 500 years, from the age of sail to the modern Royal Navy. Free entry and rich in interactive displays.

properties.name: National Museum of the Royal Navy

activities.title: Submarine Museum (HMS Alliance)
activities.description: Cross to Gosport on the ferry to visit the Royal Navy Submarine Museum. Clamber inside HMS Alliance, a real Cold War submarine, and trace the history of underwater warfare.

activities.title: Explore Action Stations
activities.description: A hands-on interactive Royal Navy attraction at the Historic Dockyard. Pilot a helicopter simulator, experience a commando assault course and learn what life in the modern Navy is really like.

activities.title: Boathouse 4 — see boats being built
activities.description: A working heritage boatyard inside the Historic Dockyard where traditional wooden boat-building and restoration skills are kept alive. Watch craftspeople at work up close.

activities.title: Harbour Tour by Boat
activities.description: A 45-minute boat trip around one of Europe's greatest naval bases. See warships, submarines and historic vessels from the water — the best way to appreciate the scale of the dockyard.

activities.title: Royal Marines Museum
activities.description: Now integrated into the National Museum of the Royal Navy at the Historic Dockyard, the Royal Marines collection tells the story of the Corps from its 1664 founding to modern day.

activities.title: Climb Spinnaker Tower
activities.description: Ride the lift to 170 metres above Portsmouth Harbour for unrivalled views across the Solent, the Isle of Wight and beyond. On a clear day you can see up to 37 miles.

activities.title: Walk the Sky Deck Glass Floor
activities.description: Step out onto the glass floor at Spinnaker Tower's viewing deck and look 100 metres straight down to the quayside below. Not one for the faint-hearted.

activities.title: Shop at Gunwharf Quays
activities.description: A designer outlet centre built on a former naval armaments wharf, right on the harbour. Over 90 brands at discounted prices with the Spinnaker Tower as its dramatic backdrop.

activities.title: Eat by the Water at Gunwharf
activities.description: Gunwharf Quays has a string of waterfront restaurants and bars overlooking the Solent and the harbour. A great spot for everything from brunch to evening cocktails.

activities.title: Catch a Film at Vue Gunwharf
activities.description: A modern multiplex cinema at the heart of Gunwharf Quays, showing the latest blockbusters and special screenings.

activities.title: Stand on the Round Tower
activities.description: Climb the 15th-century Round Tower at the mouth of Portsmouth Harbour. One of the oldest fortifications in the city and a prime spot for watching ships enter and leave.

activities.title: Climb the Square Tower
activities.description: Built in 1494, the Square Tower was once a royal residence and gunpowder store. Climb it for great views over the harbour mouth and the Solent.

activities.title: Walk the Hot Walls
activities.description: Stroll along the historic sea wall at the mouth of Portsmouth Harbour. Locals swim here in summer — and a plaque marks the very spot where Nelson walked to his ship for the last time.

activities.title: Hotwalls Studios — Meet Artists
activities.description: A cluster of working artist studios built into the arches of the Old Portsmouth sea walls. Drop in to watch painters, ceramicists and makers at work and buy directly from the artist.

activities.title: Pint at the Spice Island Inn
activities.description: A historic pub right at the harbour mouth in Old Portsmouth. Sit outside with a pint and watch the ferries, yachts and naval vessels pass just metres away.

activities.title: Pint at the Still & West
activities.description: A beloved Old Portsmouth pub right on the waterfront with a spectacular deck overlooking the harbour mouth. One of the best pub views in the south of England.

activities.title: Visit Portsmouth Cathedral
activities.description: Portsmouth's Anglican cathedral, with origins going back to the 12th century. Free to enter and rich in naval monuments, memorials and stained glass.

activities.title: Royal Garrison Church Ruins
activities.description: A hauntingly atmospheric roofless church in Old Portsmouth, bombed during the Blitz and preserved as a memorial. The nave is open to the sky while the chancel remains intact.

activities.title: Quebec House on Bath Square
activities.description: A Grade I listed building on Bath Square believed to be Britain's oldest surviving seawater bathhouse. A beautifully preserved gem in the heart of Old Portsmouth.

activities.title: Find the Point Where Nelson Sailed
activities.description: A plaque on the Hot Walls marks the exact spot where Admiral Lord Nelson stepped into his barge for the last time in September 1805, to join HMS Victory before the Battle of Trafalgar.

activities.title: The D-Day Story Museum
activities.description: Home to the Overlord Embroidery — a 272-foot tapestry inspired by the Bayeux Tapestry — alongside compelling exhibits on the D-Day landings and the role Portsmouth played in Operation Overlord.

activities.title: Blue Reef Aquarium
activities.description: Walk through an underwater tunnel surrounded by rays, sharks and thousands of sea creatures. A brilliant family attraction on the Southsea seafront.

activities.title: Sit on a Stripey Deckchair
activities.description: Hire a traditional striped deckchair near Southsea Castle, face the Solent and do absolutely nothing. A quintessential British seaside experience.

activities.title: Spot the Isle of Wight on a Clear Day
activities.description: On a clear day the Isle of Wight looms large across the Solent from the Southsea seafront — look south and you can make out Ryde, Sandown and the chalk cliffs of Culver Down.

activities.title: Visit the Naval Memorial
activities.description: A striking obelisk on Southsea Common commemorating over 24,000 Royal Navy personnel lost at sea in both World Wars with no known grave. Free to visit and deeply moving.

activities.title: Eastney Beam Engine House
activities.description: A magnificent Victorian sewage pumping station with two huge James Watt beam engines still in working order. One of Portsmouth's most underrated industrial heritage gems.

activities.title: Hayling Ferry
activities.description: A 5-minute open-boat ferry crossing from Ferry Point at Eastney to Hayling Island. One of the oldest ferry crossings in England and a lovely way to arrive on the island.

activities.title: Walk Fort Cumberland
activities.description: An impressive 18th-century pentagonal artillery fort at the southeastern tip of Portsea Island. One of the finest examples of its kind in England — worth walking the exterior at low tide.

activities.title: Great Salterns Walk
activities.description: A quiet coastal park and nature area with views across to Hayling Island. Walk the paths around the former salt marsh and enjoy the birdlife and open water views.

activities.title: Eastney Lake Lap
activities.description: A peaceful harbour-side stroll around the tidal inlet at Eastney — quiet, unhurried and a world away from the bustle of the seafront.

activities.title: Langstone Harbour Kayak
activities.description: Launch from Eastney for flat-water paddling around the sheltered waters of Langstone Harbour. A brilliant way to explore the harbour's creeks, islands and birdlife from the water.

activities.title: Bransbury Park Kickabout
activities.description: A large, open grassy park near Eastney — ideal for a casual football game, frisbee or simply a run. Local and unhurried, with a genuine neighbourhood feel.

activities.title: Walk to Fort Widley
activities.description: One of the Palmerston Forts on Portsdown Hill, Fort Widley offers superb views and a fascinating insight into 19th-century defensive engineering. Walk up from Cosham for the full experience.

activities.title: Fort Purbrook Open Day
activities.description: The easternmost of the Portsdown Hill Palmerston Forts, Fort Purbrook opens its gates for guided tours. A chance to explore the tunnels and ramparts of this little-visited Victorian fort.

activities.title: Pizza at the George Inn
activities.description: A hilltop pub on Portsdown Hill with one of Portsmouth's most famous views. The pizza is excellent — but the real draw is eating it while gazing over the entire city spread below.

activities.title: Charles Dickens' Birthplace
activities.description: The tiny Georgian terraced house in Old Commercial Road where Charles Dickens was born on 7 February 1812. Now a museum furnished as it would have been in the early 19th century.

activities.title: Aspex Gallery
activities.description: A free contemporary art gallery at Gunwharf Quays showing cutting-edge exhibitions by emerging and established artists. One of the south coast's most respected independent galleries.

activities.title: Kings Theatre Show
activities.description: An Edwardian theatre in Southsea presenting a year-round programme of drama, musicals, ballet, comedy and the city's beloved annual pantomime.

activities.title: New Theatre Royal
activities.description: A beautifully restored Victorian theatre in the city centre, hosting drama, opera, comedy and community productions in an intimate 500-seat auditorium.

activities.title: Gig at the Wedgewood Rooms
activities.description: A legendary intimate music venue on Albert Road that has launched some of Britain's biggest acts. A must-visit for live music lovers — check the listings and book early.

activities.title: Comedy at the Guildhall
activities.description: Portsmouth's grandest venue hosts big-name comedy, concerts and shows. The neo-classical Guildhall is an impressive building in its own right — check what's on before you visit.

activities.title: Film at No.6 Cinema
activities.description: An independent cinema located inside the Historic Dockyard showing art-house, classic and independent films in a unique setting. The most atmospheric cinema in Portsmouth.

activities.title: See a Band at the Pyramids
activities.description: The Pyramids Centre on the Southsea seafront is Portsmouth's largest live music and entertainment venue, hosting touring acts and club nights throughout the year.

activities.title: Pie & Vinyl
activities.description: A uniquely Portsmouth institution on Albert Road — a record shop that also serves proper pies and mash. Browse vinyl, eat well and soak up the best of Southsea's independent spirit.

activities.title: Brunch at Southsea Coffee Co.
activities.description: One of Southsea's most popular independent cafés on Osborne Road — excellent coffee, generous brunches and a warm neighbourhood atmosphere.

activities.title: Tea at the Tenth Hole
activities.description: A charming tearoom beside the pitch and putt at Canoe Lake — the perfect place to recover from a round of golf with a pot of tea and a slice of cake.

activities.title: Fish and Chips on the Prom
activities.description: The essential Portsmouth experience — proper fish and chips eaten out of paper while sitting on a bench facing the Solent. The cold sea air makes them taste even better.

activities.title: Cocktail at the American Bar
activities.description: A classic Old Portsmouth bar with a distinguished naval history, serving cocktails and spirits in a characterful setting just a stone's throw from the harbour.

activities.title: Sunday Roast at the Pembroke
activities.description: A tucked-away gem of a pub in Old Portsmouth serving hearty Sunday roasts. The kind of local that rewards those who know where to look.

activities.title: Coffee at Hampshire Boulangerie
activities.description: A French-style bakery in Southsea turning out exceptional pastries, sourdough and coffee. The kind of place that makes Saturday mornings worth getting up for.

activities.title: Beach Café Breakfast
activities.description: Start the day at one of the seafront café-bars right on the Southsea promenade. Eggs, bacon and a flat white with the sea right in front of you — hard to beat.

activities.title: Curry on Albert Road
activities.description: Albert Road is lined with independent restaurants from around the world. The curry houses here are particularly well regarded — an ideal end to an evening in Southsea.

activities.title: Ice Cream at Knight & Lee Corner
activities.description: Grab a scoop from one of the ice cream vendors at the Palmerston Road end of Southsea's shopping parade — a classic stop before or after a browse around the shops.

activities.title: Browse Albert Road Indies
activities.description: Southsea's most characterful street is packed with independent record shops, vintage clothing, vegan cafés and quirky gift stores. A browser's paradise.

activities.title: Castle Road Treasure Hunt
activities.description: A short street in Southsea with a cluster of antique dealers, second-hand shops and independent boutiques. Perfect for an afternoon of rummaging.

activities.title: Marmion Road for Cards & Gifts
activities.description: A quaint Southsea shopping street with independent gift shops, card stores, a florist and the Brewhouse & Kitchen craft beer pub. Perfect for a leisurely wander.

activities.title: Commercial Road High Street
activities.description: Portsmouth's main pedestrianised shopping street in the city centre, lined with high street names, markets and the covered Cascades shopping centre.

activities.title: Palmerston Road Wander
activities.description: Southsea's main shopping parade, with a good mix of independent traders alongside familiar names. The pedestrianised street is at its best on sunny afternoons.

activities.title: Round-the-Walls Walk
activities.description: Loop the entire Old Portsmouth fortifications — from the Camber Dock around the Hot Walls, up past the Round Tower and back. A short but richly historic circular walk.

activities.title: Solent Way Coastal Walk
activities.description: Part of the 60-mile long-distance Solent Way path runs through Portsmouth and Southsea, following the coastline with excellent sea views throughout.

activities.title: Bandstand to Pier Sunset Stroll
activities.description: Walk the seafront promenade from the Southsea bandstand to South Parade Pier at dusk as the lights come on along the prom and the sky turns pink over the Solent.

activities.title: Cycle the Seafront End-to-End
activities.description: Ride the dedicated cycle path the full length of the Southsea seafront from Clarence Pier all the way to Eastney and back. Flat, fast and with the sea beside you the whole way.

activities.title: Walk to Old Portsmouth at Low Tide
activities.description: At low tide, explore the foreshore below the Hot Walls and around Bath Square — ancient stonework, pottery shards and centuries of harbour history revealed by the retreating sea.

activities.title: Cosham to Portsdown Ridge Walk
activities.description: Climb up from Cosham village to the top of Portsdown Hill on foot, following the ridge path with panoramic views opening up over the whole of Portsmouth and the Solent.

activities.title: Find the Sherlock Holmes Statue
activities.description: Arthur Conan Doyle lived and practised medicine in Portsmouth — and a statue of his most famous creation stands outside the City Museum. A must for Holmes fans.

activities.title: Spot Street Art on Albert Road
activities.description: Albert Road and the surrounding Southsea backstreets are home to an ever-changing collection of murals and street art. A worthwhile wander with your eyes up.

activities.title: Victorian Shelter on Eastney Prom
activities.description: A beautifully weathered cast-iron Victorian seafront shelter on the Eastney promenade — salt-blasted, slightly forgotten and absolutely worth seeking out.

activities.title: Submarine Memorial Garden
activities.description: A quiet and moving memorial garden near the seafront commemorating submariners lost on patrol. A hidden and contemplative corner of the city.

activities.title: Falklands Memorial
activities.description: A sombre and powerful memorial on Southsea Common to the Task Force personnel killed in the 1982 Falklands War. Portsmouth was the home port for much of the fleet.

activities.title: Watch the Brittany Ferry Leave
activities.description: The giant Brittany Ferries ships departing for Caen, Cherbourg and St Malo are an impressive sight. Watch from the Round Tower or Hot Walls as they pass just metres away.

activities.title: Sunset from the Round Tower
activities.description: The Round Tower at the harbour mouth is arguably the best free viewpoint in the city. Come at sunset and watch the sky turn over the Solent as ships pass in silhouette.

activities.title: Catch the Gosport Ferry
activities.description: A 5-minute passenger ferry crossing of Portsmouth Harbour to Gosport — the shortest sea crossing in Britain and one of the most atmospheric. Run continuously all day.

activities.title: Day Trip to Isle of Wight
activities.description: Jump on a Wightlink catamaran from Portsmouth Harbour to Ryde in just 22 minutes. The island offers beaches, cycling, walking, Osborne House and Cowes — a full day's adventure.

activities.title: Hovertravel to Ryde
activities.description: The only scheduled hovercraft passenger service in Europe runs from Southsea to Ryde on the Isle of Wight in 10 minutes. A genuinely unique and thrilling way to travel.

activities.title: Beer at the Brewhouse & Kitchen
activities.description: A craft microbrewery and pub on Marmion Road brewing its own ales on site. Tour the brewery, try a tasting paddle and stay for a proper meal.

activities.title: Watch the City Wake Up from Spinnaker
activities.description: Buy an early-morning ticket for the Spinnaker Tower and have the viewing deck almost entirely to yourself. Watch Portsmouth come to life 170 metres below as the harbour slowly fills with activity.
